# Demetri Hodges

> Demetri Hodges is a builder, researcher, and technologist exploring the intersection of intelligence, software, and human systems.

Driven by curiosity and a bias toward building, Demetri spends his time creating products, conducting research, and experimenting with new forms of intelligence—from software agents and AI infrastructure to economic systems and human-computer interaction. He is drawn to simple, intuitive design and the belief that sophistication is best expressed through clarity.

Personal site: https://demetri.xyz/

## Projects

- [Obius](https://obius.io): "Architect your thoughts." Node-based thinking and notes app with structure-aware AI, live reusable concepts, immutable versioning, and on-device storage. iOS, with macOS coming soon. Free tier; Pro at $9.99/mo.
- [Bouncr](https://thebouncr.com): "Your paywall should haggle." Drop-in AI pricing-negotiation layer for subscription apps; a deterministic policy engine sets every price so the LLM can't be talked below your floor. Stripe settlement, MCP-native.
- [Dromo](https://www.dromo.fit): "Run to the beat. Hit your pace." Pace-adaptive running music for iOS (coming soon) that locks your library's tempo to your cadence; on-device analysis, BPM-only data leaves the phone.
- [RRSRCH](https://rrsrch.com): Independent research lab founded by Demetri Hodges.

## Writing

- [The Fairness–Discoverability Ceiling](https://demetri.xyz/papers/the-fairness-discoverability-ceiling.pdf): A worked negative result in long-horizon agent evaluation — why "spontaneously hard," "fair to grade," and "deterministically gradeable" can't hold at once (June 2026).
- [The Test That Broke Because the AI Was Right](https://demetri.xyz/papers/the-test-that-broke.pdf): The accessible story of an AI eval that broke because the model was reasoning correctly — on fairness and self-deception (June 2026).
- [The Lies I Loved](https://demetri.xyz/papers/the-lies-i-loved.pdf): Meditations on time, truth, and the cost of self-deception (June 2026).
- [The Great Forgetting](https://demetri.xyz/papers/the-great-forgetting.pdf): On knowledge, wisdom, and the cost of infinite access (June 2026).
- [The Doldrums](https://demetri.xyz/papers/the-doldrums.pdf): On consciousness, cognition, and human succession (June 2026).
- [Mass Drift Theory](https://demetri.xyz/papers/Mass%20Drift%20Theory-%20A%20Macrodynamic%20Framework%20for%20Systemic%20Shifts%20in%20Collective%20Opinion.pdf): A macrodynamic framework for systemic shifts in collective opinion (May 2025).
